newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest grains futures mixed in brisk market.
newsitem.headline: Budapest grains futures mixed in brisk market.

text.p: Grains futures were mixed on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Wednesday in one of this year's busiest days for trade, dealers said.
May maize and milling wheat accounted for half of grains turnover, with players seeking to close positions before contracts mature next week.
"Position-closing was triggered both by those who wanted to lock in profits and those who were afraid of further price rises despite today's halt," said Gyorgy Varga of OTP Forex.
May maize rose 100 forints per tonne to 20,200 forints with 1,392 contracts traded.
Total grains turnover was 1.58 billion forints, or 3,436 contracts, compared with Tuesday's 822.8 million.
The BCE said today's turnover was the year's highest in volume terms and among the first three in forints.
July maize was the second most popular maturity with 716 contracts changing hands. It closed at 19,900 forints, up 300.

Milling wheat futures also ended higher for the nearest maturities while the deferred ones moved lower. October, which was freed up on Monday, dropped 450 forints to 27,050, December lost 680 to end at 27,800 and March went down 1,500 forints to 28,500.
